words.en: by the blast of his breath
words.g: m. instr. sg.; compound (see Samāsa)
pronominal adjective अन्य, m. acc. pl.; object of पातयामास
causative of √पत् (bhvādi, 1P ‘to fall’), stem पातय-, liṭ (periphrastic perfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada; subject महिषासुरः from 3.21
n. loc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa)

sandhi.note: Final t becomes d before a vowel. Inside कांश्चित् itself the n of कान् meets the c of चित् and becomes ṃś (नश्छव्यप्रशान्, 8.3.7), as in कांश्चित् at the head of 3.22.
Final n before the n of नादेन simply stands; the Gita Press writes the two words together.

samasa.sense: by the gale of his snorting breath
samasa.alt: Also possible as a karmadhāraya, निःश्वासः एव पवनः ‘the breath which is a wind’; the sense is the same. निःश्वास is itself a prefixed noun (निस् + √श्वस् + घञ्), not a compound.

samasa.literal: on the surface of the earth

morph.note: Periphrastic perfect of the causative: पातय- + आम् + the perfect of √अस् (आस). Causatives and other derived stems form their perfect this way. ‘Made to fall’ = ‘felled’.
The indefinite pronoun: किम् with the particle चित्, declined in its first part (कः → कश्चित्, कान् → कांश्चित्). With अपरान् and अन्यान् it gives the distributive ‘some … others … others again’.
Action noun in -अन (ल्युट्) from √भ्रम् ‘to wander, whirl’; neuter.

mantras.anvaya: (महिषासुरः) कांश्चित् वेगेन, अपरान् नादेन भ्रमणेन च, अन्यान् निःश्वासपवनेन भूतले पातयामास।
mantras.anvaya_en: पातयामास is the verb for the whole list begun in 3.22: the accusatives there (कांश्चित्, अपरान्, अन्यान्, the participles ताडितान्, विदारितान्) and here all depend on it, each with its own instrumental of means.
mantras.lit: Some by (his) charge, others by (his) bellowing and whirling, and others by the wind of (his) breath, he felled on the ground.
mantras.tr: Some he threw to the ground by the force of his charge, others with his bellowing and his wheeling about, and others again with the blast of his breath.
mantras.tr_note: The verb completes the sentence begun in 3.22; the subject, Mahiṣāsura, is named in 3.21.

comm.t: The buffalo’s rampage through the Goddess’s gaṇas ends: every part of the animal — speed, voice, motion, breath — is a weapon. The single verb पातयामास gathers the long list of 3.22–23.

The gaṇas he fells were born from the Goddess’s own breath in battle (निःश्वासान् मुमुचे … त एव सद्यः सम्भूता गणाः, 2.52–53). Here the buffalo fells them with the wind of his breath: breath against breath, before the duel itself begins.

words.g: absolutive (ल्यप्) of the causative of नि + √पत्; agent is सः असुरः

words.en: the army of the Pramathas (the Goddess’s troops)

√कृ (tanādi, 8U), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, ātmanepada
indeclinable (adverb of time, तद् + तसिल्)
f. nom. sg. of अम्बिका; subject of चक्रे

sandhi.note: Final m stays m before a vowel and is written joined to it (anusvāra only before a consonant, मोऽनुस्वारः 8.3.23).
Before a vowel the special rule for सः (6.1.132) does not apply; -aḥ + a- gives -o ’-, the initial a marked by avagraha.

samasa.sense: of the Goddess (whose mount is the lion)

morph.note: Imperfect ātmanepada of √धाव् (धावति / धावते), with the augment between prefix and root: अभि + अ + धाव + त; इ before अ becomes य (इको यणचि, 6.1.77). The same form stands in 3.6 (अभ्यधावत तां देवीम्).
Absolutive of the causative stem पातय-: a prefixed verb takes -य (ल्यप्) for -त्वा, and the causative -अय- is dropped before it.
Perfect ātmanepada of √कृ. कोपं चक्रे, ‘made anger’, is the regular idiom for ‘became angry’; 3.28 has the imperfect कोपं … अकरोत्.

mantras.anvaya: सः असुरः प्रमथानीकं निपात्य महादेव्याः सिंहं हन्तुम् अभ्यधावत। ततः अम्बिका कोपं चक्रे।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two sentences: the asura’s charge (absolutive, object, infinitive of purpose, verb) and the Goddess’s answer (कोपं चक्रे).
mantras.lit: Having struck down the army of the Pramathas, that asura rushed forward to kill the great Goddess’s lion. Then Ambikā became angry.
mantras.tr: Having cut down the Goddess’s host, the demon charged to kill the great Goddess’s lion. At that, Ambikā grew angry.

comm.t: With the gaṇas down, Mahiṣa goes for the lion, the Goddess’s mount (given her by Himavān, 2.29). The attack on her vāhana is what turns her anger on him; from here the duel is between the two of them.
प्रमथ ‘tormentor’ is a name used elsewhere for Śiva’s troops; here it names the gaṇas the Goddess produced from her breath (2.53).

words.en: pounding the earth’s surface with his hooves

sandhi.note: Final t (voiced to d) becomes the nasal n before the nasal m.

sandhi.type: consonant sandhi (n before a vowel; n + c)
sandhi.note: पर्वतान् joins उच्चान् unchanged (after a long ā the n is not doubled); the n of उच्चान् before c becomes ṃś.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi containing a tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa (खुरक्षुण्ण = खुरैः क्षुण्णम्) and a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (महीतल = मह्याः तलम्)
samasa.literal: by whom the surface of the earth was crushed with hooves
samasa.sense: tearing up the ground with his hooves
samasa.alt: Also read खुरक्षुण्णं महीतलं यस्य सः ‘whose ground is hoof-crushed’; the same picture.

morph.note: Perfect of √क्षिप्: reduplication चि- (क्ष् → च्) and guṇa of the root vowel in the singular (क्षेप).
Perfect of √नद् with vṛddhi of the root a in the third singular (ना-द).
क्षुण्ण is the past participle of √क्षुद् (rudhādi, ‘to crush’): the d of the root becomes n before the -na suffix, and n → ṇ after kṣ.

mantras.anvaya: महावीर्यः सः अपि कोपात् खुरक्षुण्णमहीतलः (सन्) शृङ्गाभ्याम् उच्चान् पर्वतान् चिक्षेप ननाद च।
mantras.anvaya_en: One subject with two epithets; two finite verbs joined by च … च.
mantras.lit: He too, of great might, out of anger, crushing the surface of the earth with (his) hooves, both hurled lofty mountains with (his) two horns and bellowed.
mantras.tr: He too, in his fury, mighty, churning the earth with his hooves, tossed high mountains with his horns and bellowed.

comm.t: Anger answers anger: the Goddess’s कोप (3.24) is met by his (कोपात्). The buffalo’s violence now reaches the scale of the world — earth, mountains, and in the next verses the ocean and the clouds. Verses 3.25–27 strike each region in turn: earth, water, then the sky.

words.g: f. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies मही
f. nom. sg. of मही; subject of व्यशीर्यत
pronoun तद्, m. gen. sg.; construed with the first member of the compound (‘his rush and whirling’)
वि + √शॄ (kryādi, 9P ‘to crush’), passive stem शीर्य- (यक्), laṅ (imperfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, ātmanepada; intransitive sense
n. instr. sg. of लाङ्गूल
past participle (क्त) of आ + √हन्, m. nom. sg.; qualifies अब्धिः
indeclinable (conjunction)
m. nom. sg. of अब्धि (‘water-holder’); subject of प्लावयामास
causative of √प्लु (bhvādi, 1Ā ‘to float’), stem प्लावय-, liṭ (periphrastic perfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
indeclinable (सर्व + तसिल्)

sandhi.note: a + ā → ā twice (लाङ्गूलेनाहतः, चाब्धिः); between them the visarga of आहतः becomes s before c and the s becomes ś (आहतश्च).
The prefix वि before the augment अ becomes व्य.

samasa.vigraha: वेगश्च भ्रमणं च वेगभ्रमणे; ताभ्यां विक्षुण्णा
samasa.type: tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa whose first member is an itaretara dvandva
samasa.sense: pounded to pieces by his charging and wheeling
samasa.alt: वेगभ्रमण may also be a tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa, वेगेन भ्रमणम् ‘whirling at speed’. The dvandva is preferred because 3.23 lists वेगेन and भ्रमणेन as two separate means.

morph.note: √शॄ forms its passive शीर्यते (ॠ → ईर्); the passive of this root is regularly used for ‘to fall apart, wither’. Imperfect with augment: वि + अ + शीर्य + त.
Periphrastic perfect of the causative of √प्लु: ‘made (things) float’, i.e. flooded. No object is stated; सर्वतः gives its extent.
Past participle of आ + √हन्: the nasal of the root is lost before -त (हत).

mantras.anvaya: तस्य वेगभ्रमणविक्षुण्णा मही व्यशीर्यत। लाङ्गूलेन आहतः अब्धिः च सर्वतः प्लावयामास।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two clauses, earth and ocean. तस्य depends on the idea of ‘rush and whirling’ inside the compound (a genitive construed with a compound member, accepted in epic usage).
mantras.lit: The earth, crushed by his rush and whirling, split apart; and the ocean, lashed by (his) tail, flooded on every side.
mantras.tr: Pounded by his charging and wheeling, the earth broke apart; and the ocean, lashed by his tail, overflowed on every side.

comm.t: Earth and water suffer next: the ground splits under his hooves and turning, the sea spills over its shores at a blow of his tail.
A modern reading: the buffalo’s rage does not stay inside the battle. Unchecked force damages the ground everyone stands on — which is why, in this story, it has to be stopped.

repeated (vīpsā): खण्डं खण्डम् ‘piece by piece, into pieces’
√या (adādi, 2P ‘to go’), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa bahuvacana, parasmaipada
m. nom. pl. of घन (lit. ‘dense’); subject of ययुः

words.en: hurled by the wind of his breath

नि + √पत् (bhvādi, 1P), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa bahuvacana, parasmaipada

sandhi.note: After a vowel other than a/ā the visarga (as ru) becomes r before a voiced sound. So निपेतुर्नभसः.
a + a → ā at both junctions.

samasa.type: tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa whose first member is a karmadhāraya (धुतशृङ्ग = धुते शृङ्गे)
samasa.sense: torn apart by his tossing horns

samasa.type: tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa whose first member is a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa
samasa.literal: thrown by the wind of breath
samasa.sense: blown away by the blast of his breath

morph.note: Perfect third plural of √या: the root ā is lost before the ending -उः (य-य्-उः).
Perfect third plural of √पत्: the root a becomes e and the reduplication is dropped (पेतुः for *पपतुः), the regular pattern for roots like पत्, पच्, नश्.
अस्त is the past participle of √अस् (divādi, ‘to throw’), not of √अस् ‘to be’.

mantras.anvaya: धुतशृङ्गविभिन्नाः घनाः च खण्डं खण्डं ययुः। श्वासानिलास्ताः अचलाः शतशः नभसः निपेतुः।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two clauses, clouds and mountains, each subject carrying a compound participle of cause.
mantras.lit: And the clouds, split by (his) tossing horns, went piece by piece; mountains thrown by the wind of (his) breath fell by the hundred from the sky.
mantras.tr: The clouds, torn by his tossing horns, were shredded to pieces, and mountains flung up by the blast of his breath came crashing down from the sky by the hundred.
mantras.tr_note: ‘Flung up’ makes explicit what अस्ताः ‘thrown’ implies, since they fall ‘from the sky’.

comm.t: The sky is struck last: the clouds are torn and mountains rain down. The picture completes the cosmic scale of 3.25–27, after which the narrator turns to the Goddess (3.28). अचल, ‘the immovable’, is a common word for a mountain; the paradox is deliberate — what cannot move is thrown about by his breath.
